No, that is not accurate. The validity of a residence permit in Switzerland depends on the type of permit and the purpose of stay (e.g., work, study, family reunification). There is no single rule that all permits are only valid for one year, nor is an open-ended employment contract an absolute requirement for obtaining a work permit.

For EU/EFTA citizens, the most common work permit is the B permit. Its validity can vary based on the employment contract:

- If you have a fixed-term contract, the permit is typically issued for the duration of that contract, plus a possible short extension if the contract is renewed or if you find a new job within a reasonable timeframe.
- If you have an open-ended (indefinite) contract, the permit is often issued for longer periods (e.g., five years) and is renewable.

However, the permit is always tied to the purpose of your stay (i.e., your employment). If you lose your job, you may need to find a new one within a certain period (usually a few months) to maintain your right to stay, or you may need to change your permit status (e.g., to a short-stay L permit or leave the country).

For precise information, always consult the official Swiss authorities, such as the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) or your local cantonal migration office, as rules can vary by canton and individual circumstances.
